name: fix-carrier-inference
problem: Conn-edge carrier inference is walk-order dependent (issues/carrier-inference-order-dependence.md): resolve.rs collects rel/conn/view defs and binds uses in one pass over sorted modules, so an edge that precedes its conn's def — in module-name order or textually within one module — finds no lane patterns, exact-lane inference silently degrades, and the author gets the engine's raw E_CARRIER_REQUIRED instead of the compiler's targeted hint. v0004 hardened the spec: Compiler.Resolver is phased into Defs (whole-model def sweep) and Uses (binding against the complete table). This plan makes the code match it.

technology_stack.provenance: the resolver being fixed lives there; the workspace toolchain is a given

technology_stack.tech: cargo test — resolve.rs tests mod plus tests/source_e2e.rs
technology_stack.provenance: the suites the requirement's regression tests extend

architecture_summary.role: phased binding: Defs sweeps every module's rel/conn/view defs into the def table, then Uses binds edges, apps and carriers against the completed table
the whole-model def sweep — all modules, all textual positions, before any use
binds node bodies, opens, edges, apps; carrier inference reads complete lane patterns; the def-less preset path unchanged

stack_mapping.tech: collect_uses walking DefNode/Open/Edge/App only, after the sweep

scenarios: cargo test --workspace is green, including four new order regressions: conn def in module z used with inferred carriers in module a; def textually after its first use in one module; def-less conn edges unchanged; bit-identical batches under module renaming.

The self-model's workaround is obsolete for inference: renamed to src/agent.arch (sorting before conns.arch) the model compiles clean under archi check — the bootstrap's original failure. The rename itself stays deferred: verifying it surfaced issues/canonical-render-edge-order-depends-on-module-names.md (the canonical render orders edges by module walk, so the rename reorders an identical model's render); operator.arch's comment now points there.

The bootstrap repro now compiles: scratch project with def conn invoke in zconns.arch and an inferred-carrier edge in aedge.arch passes archi check; omitting a genuinely uninferable carrier yields the compiler hint (name it — `invoke(->X)`) at the edge span, not the engine's JSON error.
